newsitem.title: USA: Frustrated moose damage planes with antlers.
newsitem.headline: Frustrated moose damage planes with antlers.

text.p: Two young bull moose trying to shed their antlers have caused $20,000 worth of damage to small planes parked at Anchorage International Airport by banging their heads against the aircraft.
Owners of small planes parked at the airport's floatplane centre have found their aircraft dented, punctured and scratched.
State biologists are planning to shoot the bulls with a tranquilliser and remove their antlers, either by shaking or sawing them off.

Older bull moose usually drop their antlers after the fall mating season. But the young moose, about two years old, were still carrying their antlers, said Rick Sinnott, a biologist with the Alaska Department of Fish and Game.
He said they were banging their antlers against the planes to try to knock them off. Plane owners had initially been baffled by the damage.

"In every case they knew it wasn't vandalism because there were no human tracks around, but there were moose tracks walking up to the plane," Sinnott said. One of the animals was later seen hitting a plane.
Up to a dozen moose live near the airport and sometimes meander through said Sinnott, who added that he had never known any to damage planes.
